chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has money due from another, and the debtor is insolvent, so he buys a sale on credit from a man, on the condition that I guarantee to the creditor that he will pay what is due to me. He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm in it (permissible)
key_terms.مُعْسِرٌ: Insolvent person (one who cannot pay debts)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to guarantee a debt when buying a credit sale from an insolvent debtor?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a specific credit sale structure where the original creditor guarantees the debtor's payment to a third-party buyer, demonstrating the flexibility of *kafalah* (guarantee) in commercial transactions. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on facilitating trade and resolving insolvency without invalidating the underlying contract, provided the guarantee is clearly stipulated. It serves as a foundational precedent for modern Islamic finance instruments involving debt trading and suretyship.
